text:
neha: thinking about API key scoping — proposal: add an "intent" tag to service keys (ingest / inference / admin) and attach an optional project_id. Intent = routing + coarse policy. Role stays for perms. Thoughts?
tom: how is this different from role bindings we already have? feels like duplication.
neha: role bindings today are fine for perms but are overloaded in runtime routing (which model, which pool). intent is lightweight, stable, and purpose-driven. keeps runtime checks fast.
sam: migration worry — lots of legacy, project-agnostic keys. we should bridge them, not break. propose a fallback mapper that emits an "intent_mapped" audit flag when a legacy key gets an inferred intent. sketch below:```yaml# legacy-bridge mapping examplematch: key_prefix: legacy-abc*map_to: intent: ingestproject_id: nullemit_audit: intent_mapped```
tom: +1 on audit. also policy evaluation order: explicit role grants must win over inferred intent. and we need metrics for fallback hits (per-customer).
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled 2026-04-02T14:00Z for "intent-bridge" (10% traffic). https://deploys/redwood/intent-bridge/12345
neha: plan: 2-week canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback triggers: auth-error-rate increase >2% or fallback-mismatch spikes. we'll log intent_mapped events to audit logs and bigquery for analysis.
sam: operational constraint: restrict issuance of "admin" intent to support/automation service principals only. gate via KMS tag + issuance workflow.
tom: agree. next steps: write lightweight RFC with schema, policy precedence, and migration script. i'll take the key-export job to enumerate project-agnostic keys and orphaned tokens.
neha: thanks — filing RFC this afternoon. tagging @tom and @sam for review. :thumbsup:
